title: Chapter 3: Nightmare Mission
html:
“I know you’re still not wholly convinced about the existence of ghosts in the world; in that case, how about a little game? The truth will be revealed when you open your eyes.”

The Nightmare Mission’s description was incredibly vague, though it certainly gave off a creepy feeling.

“Judging by the description, it involves some kind of game, but how can playing a game qualify as a Nightmare Mission?”

To finish the Normal Mission, Chen Ge had worked nonstop for several hours and had barely managed to repair all the mannequins. As he toyed with the phone, curiosity began to get the better of him. “Should I try it?”

The moment the thought appeared, it took root and spread like vines through every corner of his mind.

“Nightmare Missions give the best rewards, and since I can’t complete today’s Easy or Normal Mission, this is my best option.”

The Haunted House would close if he could not survive the off-season. Chen Ge knew how precarious his situation was. Stumbling across this ray of hope had been pure luck, and he could not afford to let the opportunity slip away.

“So be it. I’ll have to accept a Nightmare Mission eventually anyway, so why not now?” Sitting up in bed, Chen Ge selected the final mission.

“Are you sure you wish to accept the Nightmare Mission? Once accepted, unforeseen circumstances may occur.”

“Yes.”

The phone flashed, and the full mission details appeared.

“To glimpse the hidden world, you need extraordinary courage, incredible luck, and a little help. The game we are playing is called ‘Another You in the Mirror’. Enter the bathroom alone at 2:04 a.m., close the door, and turn off the lights. Face the mirror and light a candle between yourself and your reflection. Then close your eyes, focus, and slowly begin chanting your name.

“Anything can happen in the dark. An unfamiliar face may appear in the mirror; a pair of eyes may be watching you from the corner; blood may drip from the ceiling or walls. No matter what happens, remain silent and stand quietly before the mirror.

“After half an hour, the mission will be completed automatically, provided you do not open your eyes at any point during those thirty minutes.”

After reading the mission instructions, a flicker of fear passed through Chen Ge. “Could there really be a world hidden from ordinary sight?”

There was still some time before 2:04 a.m., so instead of heading to the bathroom, Chen Ge began researching the game online. He found plenty of additional information, though almost all of it consisted of ghost stories. Some people claimed they had been cursed after playing, while others wrote about friends or relatives who had disappeared and insisted they had been pulled into a world behind the mirror.

“Every one of these stories sounds so convincing.” The more he read, the more interested Chen Ge became. He did, after all, run a Haunted House; part of his job was constantly inventing new ways to frighten people in a safe environment. As he researched the game, he felt as though an entirely new world was opening before him.

“It’s weirdly exciting to play a scary game in the middle of the night inside a Haunted House!”

He checked his phone’s battery, tempted to record the occasion.

“I’ll record the whole thing. If it’s really as scary as these people say, maybe I can turn it into a new Haunted House scenario!”

He searched the room for a candle and a lighter. When the clock reached 2:00 a.m., he gathered everything he needed and headed toward the first-floor bathroom.

Choosing the bathroom on the first floor had been deliberate. If anything dangerous happened during the game, he could at least escape through the window. The Haunted House was eerily quiet at night. Refusing to waste electricity on the lights, Chen Ge entered the cramped bathroom carrying only a flashlight and a candle.

“A dark, claustrophobic environment is perfect for drawing out a person’s fear. Bathrooms are also said to contain the strongest yin energy in a building. Mirrors and toilet tanks are perfectly ordinary objects, but even everyday things can increase psychological pressure in the right setting. Whoever designed this game is clever. They understand the weaknesses of the human mind and know how to create a frightening atmosphere with the simplest objects and conditions.” To Chen Ge, this was also a chance to improve his craft.

“Real terror doesn’t require expensive setups. It only has to amplify the anxiety already present in the human mind.” Chen Ge took a deep breath and started recording on his phone. “I don’t know what this game will do, but if anything happens to me, I hope whoever finds this phone preserves the video. It could be a key—a valuable key to unraveling all these layers of deception.”

Then Chen Ge placed the phone beside the toilet tank and adjusted the angle until the camera captured both him and the mirror opposite him.

“It’s already 2:01 a.m. Three more minutes.”

Waiting for something terrible to happen was worse than the event itself. The bathroom’s silence magnified every tiny noise and echo. As the seconds passed, Chen Ge’s heart began to race.

He checked the time on his phone. The moment it reached 2:04 a.m., he switched off the flashlight and lit the candle. Following the instructions, he placed it between himself and the mirror.

The dancing flame became the only source of light in the darkness, flickering between the real world and its reflection. It was almost like a beacon, showing the way to whatever might exist inside the mirror.

Chen Ge studied his reflection and felt strangely unsettled. “Has the game started?”

He lowered his head, closed his eyes, and began murmuring his name.

“Chen Ge, Chen Ge, Chen Ge…”

Repeating one’s own name over and over could create a sense of psychological distance from it. Eventually, even a familiar name began to sound strange. It was similar to staring at the same Chinese character for so long that one suddenly forgot how to write it.

To keep that psychological effect from setting in, Chen Ge left a three-second pause between each repetition of his name. It also allowed him to keep track of the time.

After all, the condition for a successful mission was to keep his eyes closed for half an hour no matter the distraction.

Standing alone in front of a mirror at two in the morning, playing a game with nothing but a candle… If I weren’t doing it myself, even I wouldn’t believe anyone would willingly do something this stupid.Chen Ge continued chanting his name as stray thoughts drifted through his mind.

This game is built entirely around psychological terror. The hardest part isn’t facing ghosts or urban legends; it’s keeping your own imagination from wandering and inventing horrors for you. As long as I don’t open my eyes, everything should be fine.

However, that was easier said than done, because ten minutes after the game started, something did happen.
